purpose: Bring your export: map an SCDPS crash export (master file / TR-310 fields) to CrashIQ's crash keys. Column names are SCDPS's own, from its CC BY 4.0 'SCDPS Collisions' layer schema; the person-level names are from the Spartanburg County layer built from the same TR-310 data.

crash.lon: Longitude (decimal_degrees_longitude; packed 'longitude' has no minus sign)
crash.primary_road: Street, else RouteCategory + RouteNum (on_route_*): Interstate -> I, US Primary -> US, SC Primary -> SC
crash.sec_distance: base_distance_offset, MILES (0.01, 0.1, 0.5, 1); not in the SCDPS dashboard layer
crash.sec_direction: offset_direction N/S/E/W. Meaning unverified: applying it from the base point made long offsets worse (see sc-import.md)
crash.city_name: not given; Agency names the police department (e.g. GREER POLICE DEPARTMENT)
crash.collision_type: not in the SCDPS layer (FirstHarmfulEvent / MostHarmfulEvent are events, not manner of collision); 'collision_type' in the county layer is the severity class

severity.crash_level_from_counts: K if NumberOfFatalities > 0, else A if Suspected_Serious_Injuries > 0, else B if Suspected_Minor_Injuries > 0, else C if Possible_Injuries > 0, else O
severity.severity_note: KABCO as SCDPS gives it. Older TR-310 words (Incapacitating / Non-Incapacitating) are A / B; GPATS also uses Serious / Minor Injury for the newer reports. Blank = U, injury level not reported.
